IR.rationale: A rising 5-year yield relative to fed funds signals that markets are pricing a faster US tightening path. That tightens global dollar liquidity and weighs on EM equity valuations, as in taper-type repricings.

B.rationale: Strong recent high-yield returns indicate that risk appetite is already priced in. Short-horizon reversal in risk assets makes this state informative about subsequent EM returns.

V.rationale: Elevated equity volatility together with high policy uncertainty marks periods of elevated risk premia. Those premia tend to be earned through higher subsequent returns once the fear subsides.

AP.rationale: A strong recent US market return tends to partially reverse at weekly-to-quarterly horizons. Global equity co-movement transmits this reversal to EM indices.

ST.rationale: Outperformance of profitable firms reflects defensive, quality-seeking positioning. That positioning is associated with depressed risk-asset prices and higher expected returns afterwards.

FX.rationale: Broad dollar strength combined with a weak commodity currency is the classic EM risk-off and funding-tightening state. It moves EM equity expected returns through the dollar-funding channel.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity price gains improve terms of trade and earnings for the many commodity-exporting emerging markets.

MC.rationale: Tight US financial conditions restrict cross-border credit and risk-taking capacity. This is associated with weaker subsequent EM equity returns.

ENDG.rationale: Short-horizon returns of country indices show mild reversal after unusually strong recent performance.

IR.rationale: A flattening curve signals growth concerns or tightening. Either tends to precede higher risk-asset volatility.

B.rationale: Simultaneous losses in US high-yield and EM sovereign bonds signal a credit and EM funding shock. Equity volatility typically follows such shocks beyond what its own past already implies.

V.rationale: High implied volatility across equity and safe-haven gold markets carries forward-looking information about broad uncertainty. That information is not yet in realised EM variance.

AP.rationale: Through the leverage and volatility-feedback effect, joint declines in EM and US equities raise subsequent volatility.

ST.rationale: Strong profitability-factor returns reflect flight to quality. Such flights coincide with stress episodes that precede higher volatility.

FX.rationale: A risk-off dollar rally tightens EM financial conditions. It is followed by turbulence in EM assets.

COM.rationale: Commodity selloffs hit exporter economies and signal global demand fears. Both raise future EM equity volatility.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions predict elevated future volatility as intermediaries' risk-bearing capacity falls.

ENDG.rationale: Variance is persistent but mean-reverting. When recent variance is very high, the excess over its own-history forecast tends to be negative.

IR.rationale: A bear steepening, with intermediate and long yields rising relative to policy rates, resembles a duration selloff. Such selloffs trigger EM outflows and sharp drawdowns.

B.rationale: Widening corporate credit spreads signal rising default risk and falling risk appetite. This raises the odds of a large EM equity loss.

V.rationale: Elevated implied volatility in oil and gold reflects cross-asset macro uncertainty that is highly relevant to commodity-linked EM economies. It widens the left tail.

AP.rationale: Recent EM equity weakness raises conditional volatility and the chance of further large declines through volatility clustering.

ST.rationale: US equity style factors carry little direct mechanism for EM left-tail events.

FX.rationale: Dollar strength with commodity-currency weakness is the archetypal EM stress state. It raises dollar debt burdens and capital outflows.

COM.rationale: Falling oil prices damage oil-exporting emerging markets and often accompany global demand scares.

MC.rationale: Jointly tight conditions and elevated measured financial stress identify systemic stress episodes. In those episodes EM crashes are most likely.

ENDG.rationale: Large losses cluster in time, so weak recent performance raises tail-loss probability via volatility persistence.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields relative to the policy rate signal expected easing. Easier dollar liquidity can spark strong EM rallies.

B.rationale: Credit selloffs depress risk-asset prices and raise risk premia. This sets up sharp rebounds.

V.rationale: Periods of high fear and uncertainty widen the return distribution and offer high risk premia. Large relief rallies often occur from such states.

AP.rationale: Weak recent global equity performance precedes rebounds, and global equity rebounds carry EM indices.

ST.rationale: Flight-to-quality episodes depress riskier assets. Those assets can then rebound strongly.

FX.rationale: A risk-off dollar spike with a yen safe-haven bid marks capitulation-like stress. Large EM rebounds tend to follow as such moves unwind.

COM.rationale: Rising commodity prices lift terms of trade and earnings in exporter markets, increasing the chance of strong gains.

MC.rationale: Financial stress without deteriorating real activity identifies sentiment-driven selloffs. Such selloffs are prone to sharp reversals.

ENDG.rationale: Weak recent index performance raises volatility and mean-reversion potential. That increases the chance of an unusually large gain.
